sn54.8:3.2: The body might become fatigued, for example, through many hours of walking meditation. The eyes might become fatigued when focusing on an external object of meditation, such as a corpse, a light, or a color. More generally, since mindfulness of breathing focuses on the principle of life, it is nourishing and sustaining for both body and mind. It is because other meditations have certain counter-indications (see also the next Sutta) that mindfulness of breathing is recommended as generally suited for almost everyone. Nonetheless, there are certain counter-indications for any meditation. In some people, it can induce panic attacks, amplify delusional thinking or hallucinations, and strengthen anxiety or depression. Meditation is an exercise for the mind, and like physical exercise, it should only be undertaken in accordance with one’s capacity.
